title: Agent fleet controller for official CLI agents on subscriptions
description: A local, open-source supervisor for the unmodified official CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, local models through OpenCode/Ollama) run under the user's own sign-ins. It keeps an outcome ledger of every task run (task category, provider, model, reasoning effort, duration, verify-command result, review/retry count, quota-limit events and reset times), manages subscription-quota exhaustion with per-provider circuit breakers and eligible-task rerouting or queueing (budget caps are stops, never fallbacks), writes durable task checkpoints and provider-neutral handoff notes so another CLI or a local model can resume interrupted work, and learns an escalate-fast / downgrade-slow model+effort policy per task category from verifiable outcomes, in shadow mode first and enforced only after evidence. A provider-switch calibration report (from AS03) and a cross-runtime eligibility policy (the only open residual of AS05) are features. Standalone CLI first; Paperclip plugin adapter second.
original_text: Merge of AS01 (adaptive model/effort controller), AS08 (quota-aware failover + durable checkpoints) and AS03 (provider-portable competence) after competition passes R1–R5 on 2026-10-09; absorbs AS05's cross-runtime eligibility-policy residual.
target_customer: People and small teams running several official CLI coding/research agents on consumer subscriptions (Claude Max, ChatGPT Pro) plus a local model; first user is the operator (this repository and kaggle/arc3), then Paperclip, Tutti and Gas Town users.
business_model: Open source (MIT) with no hosted service in scope; monetisation hypotheses deferred — the outcome ledger is the asset a later specialist-factory or team analytics product would consume. No demand or pricing evidence yet.
narrowing_or_pivot: Not a router (commoditized), not a team OS (occupied by Paperclip and others), not a credential proxy (forbidden by Anthropic's rules). The uncovered intersection is fleet scope × machine-verifiable task outcomes × subscription quota as the binding constraint × official CLIs under the user's own login.
focused_mvp_scope: C01 outcome ledger → C02 quota manager (shadow mode) → C03 durable checkpoint and cross-provider handover → C04 learned model/effort policy → C05 provider-switch calibration report; each package has a stop rule measured on the operator's own workloads.
key_validation_test: Within six weeks on two real workloads: ≥50 ledger tasks with verifiable outcomes, ≥3 quota-limit events per week actually costing tasks, ≤30% median rework on ten handovers, and a learned policy whose verified completions per quota unit beat the static assignment. Any failed gate is recorded as a negative result and narrows the scope.
derivation_reason: Competition passes R1–R5 (2026-10-09) showed routing commoditized, team-OS occupied and quota failover demanded but served only by terms-violating proxies; the merged, terms-respecting local supervisor is the single buildable wedge.
source_note: Merged after competition passes R1–R5; see REPORT.md
